main_body: Flat sand ground patch (desert), 4x3 tiles of repeating sand texture with sparse dark and light speckles
top_band: none - flat terrain texture, no standing object; uniform sand tone L=182 with 1-row speckle accents
evidence: This is a ground terrain tile, not a standing object. The column scan shows a uniform sand tone with occasional 1-row speckles (lighter L=204, darker L=156), with no top/front structure expected. The 3/4 contract does not apply to flat ground, and nothing in it reads as an elevation or plan of an object.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours and a median of 4 per tile, against 26 per tile and 80 colours for the grass reference and 7 for the paving. Shading is shallow: one base sand tone plus one lighter and one darker speckle colour, about 3 steps against the 5-6 steps Beodeul uses. The speckles are sparse and repeat identically every 16 px, so the tiling pattern is obvious, and there is no grain or tuft variation. No flat 5x5 fills, since the speckles break the surface, and there is no outline because it is ground. It is clearly thinner than the grass reference and poorer than even the paving reference in colour count, so it fails on density and shading depth.
